## 🚚 Shopify Order → Courier Dispatch
A COD order arrives, gets checked, gets booked with the courier, and the shop owner
hears about it either way. Arabic phone digits, all 58 wilaya spellings and
COD-vs-prepaid are handled in `Validate Order`.

**Every rule in the two Code nodes is inlined from `lib/logic.js`, which 39 tests cover.**
Re-run `node build-workflow.js` after editing the logic — the nodes are generated,
never hand-typed, so the tested code and the running code cannot drift.

### The courier is a mock
Algerian couriers do not issue sandbox keys without a registered business, so
`Book With Courier` points at the *Mock Courier API* workflow.

**Swapping in a real courier is a URL change plus a field mapping.** `buildParcel`
emits `recipient` / `wilaya_code` / `cod_amount`; a real API will name those
differently, and that mapping is the one thing this repo cannot test for you.

`fullResponse: true` + `neverError: true` means a 502 arrives as **data**, so
`Read Courier Reply` classifies it instead of the run dying. That also disables
`retryOnFail` for HTTP statuses — it only fires on DNS/TCP/timeout, which is why
this node needs `onError: continueRegularOutput` as well.

### Before this can run
1. Both Telegram nodes post to chat `SET-TELEGRAM-CHAT-ID`. If that group is ever upgraded to
   a supergroup the id changes to the `-100…` form and the send starts failing.
2. The demo webhook uses **Header Auth** (credential *Wolf Demo Webhook Key*). It is
   not a secret-free endpoint: it publishes a real Telegram message. Keep the key in
   an env var when firing it on camera, and delete the webhook after recording.
3. `Shopify Trigger` is live on `orders/create` against a real store. Disable it
   before demoing, or a genuine order gets a fabricated tracking number.
